archetype.name: Pocket Passer (veteran, timing-based)
archetype.definition: An 18th-year, rhythm-and-anticipation thrower who wins from a clean pocket in McVay's structure, gets the ball out on time, and lives on the intermediate window rather than his legs.

report.headline: Volume is intact, but the arm and the deep ball are shrinking
report.take:
Stafford is still the engine of a pass-leaning Rams offense. The team's pass rate over expected ranks 5th, he is 5th in passing yards per game at 268.3, and his pace sits at 4,560 yards. Underneath the volume, though, this is a much more ordinary quarterback than the 2025 version that led the league in yards and touchdowns with an EPA per play of 0.228, 8th. This year he is at 0.094 per dropback, 21st of 47. The yardage rank is volume. The efficiency rank is the real story.

The shape of the passing game explains the gap. His intermediate work is excellent: 0.385 EPA on 66 throws at 10-19 air yards, the single most productive slice of his season. His work under 10 yards is efficient and accurate, with a 3.3 CPOE on short throws and 10 touchdowns. The deep ball has gone missing. He is 26.7% on 30 throws of 20+ yards with a -10.7 CPOE and three interceptions, and his aggressiveness has fallen 5.4 points from last year. Six of his eight interceptions have come on throws of 10+ air yards, and that is why his interception rate ranks 34th after a 2025 where he threw only 0.47 a game.

The last three games are the worrying part. His intended air yards went 6.7, 4.8, 4.9 and then 4.3 against the Chargers, and his last-three EPA per dropback is -0.024 even as his completion rate jumped to 74.7%. That is a dink-and-dunk offense, not a sharp one. Now the context lands on top of it. Stafford left Sunday with ice on his right arm, and McVay acknowledged arm soreness. That is a plausible cause for an offense that has stopped pushing the ball, not just a footnote. Davante Adams is also on IR after hamstring surgery. Adams was his most efficient target by far at 0.451 EPA per target and 22.1 total, more total EPA than Puka Nacua on 25 fewer targets.

What still holds up is the operation. He is pressured on just 15.3% of dropbacks, 4th lowest, and his 3.8% sack rate ranks 7th. The no-huddle numbers (0.418 EPA, 13.9 CPOE) show the processing is still there when the tempo lets him dictate. The career line says the interceptions are partly who he is: he has always taken risks, and 2021's 17 picks came in a title-caliber season. But a 38-year-old whose air yards are collapsing while his arm is iced is a different risk than a gunslinger's variance. Until the depth comes back, expect a high-volume, low-ceiling version of him.

strengths.title: Intermediate window is still elite
strengths.body: Throws between 10 and 19 air yards are producing 0.385 EPA per play. That is the core of his value: timing throws over linebackers and under safeties in McVay's play-action and dropback concepts. It rests on anticipation more than raw velocity, so it should survive better than the deep game. The cost is three interceptions in that band.

strengths.title: Clean pockets, few sacks
strengths.body: He is rarely pressured and rarely sacked, with a 3.8% sack rate that ranks 7th. That comes from a 2.7-second release, line play and a scheme built on defined reads. His pressure-to-sack rate has been good for two straight years, so this is stable. It keeps drives alive even when the explosive plays dry up.

strengths.title: Finishing in the red zone
strengths.body: Thirteen of his 15 touchdowns have come inside the 20, on 0.264 EPA per play with a 2.7 CPOE. His short-area accuracy carries over to the compressed field, so the touchdown production has a real foundation. The exact rate will drift, though.

concerns.title: Air yards collapsing amid arm soreness
concerns.body: His intended air yards have sat below 5 in each of the last three games, ending at 4.3 against the Chargers. His last-three EPA per dropback has fallen below zero. With McVay confirming arm soreness, the drop in depth reads less like game plan and more like a limitation. If the arm doesn't recover, the offense stays horizontal and his ceiling stays capped.

concerns.title: The deep ball is broken
concerns.body: On 30 throws of 20+ air yards he is completing 26.7% with three interceptions and negative EPA. That is a dramatic fall for a passer who has always pushed the ball. Some of it is a small sample, but it lines up with the soreness and now with Adams on IR. Don't expect a rebound before Adams returns.

concerns.title: Turnovers and third downs
concerns.body: His 2.6% interception rate ranks 34th, and his third-down EPA is -0.259 at an average of 7.3 yards to go. Interceptions are a career trait, but they doubled from last season's per-game rate. The third-down struggles fit an offense that can't threaten past the sticks. Expect partial regression on the picks. The third-down issue persists while the depth is missing.

trend.note: Weeks 2-5 carried the season, with two 18-plus EPA games. Since then his yardage, depth and EPA have slid, bottoming out with 157 yards and a -9 CPOE against the Chargers. The Rams still won three of the last five on defense.

nextGame.headline: Soft Washington pass defense, if the arm cooperates
nextGame.body:
Washington is the kind of defense that props up a quarterback's numbers. It ranks 21st in pass EPA allowed, gives up 281 passing yards a game to quarterbacks (28th) and 2.29 touchdowns (27th), and it is the league's strongest pass funnel. Offenses throw 7.7 points more often than expected against it, which fits a Rams offense that already leans pass. The one place Washington holds up is short, at -0.064 EPA, 6th. That is exactly where Stafford has been living. The deep area is where it bleeds, at 0.551 EPA, 20th, and he hasn't been able to reach it. Whether he takes those shots is the real test of the arm.

Availability tilts both ways. Washington is without Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw, with Jer'Zhan Newton also on IR. That guts its interior rush and should keep his pockets as clean as usual against a defense already 23rd in sack rate. On his side, Adams is out and Colby Parkinson is out, with Terrance Ferguson possibly back at practice. Tyler Higbee becomes the tight-end option against a defense that has let TE1s score 9.1 PPR over their average, worst in the league. Stafford himself is listed Questionable with the arm. The Rams are 5.5-point road favorites, and a lead could shorten his workload.

keyMatchups.title: Stafford's arm vs. Washington's leaky deep coverage
keyMatchups.body: Washington allows big EPA on deep throws, but Stafford is 26.7% on them and his air yards have shrunk for three straight games. If he attacks downfield and connects, it signals the soreness is managed. If not, the matchup's best edge goes unused.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted Washington interior rush
keyMatchups.body: With Payne and Kinlaw out, the push up the middle that disrupts timing throwers should be lighter. Washington's sack rate ranks 23rd, and Stafford is already one of the least-pressured passers. Expect long, clean drives.

keyMatchups.title: Higbee against the worst TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Washington has allowed TE1s the most production over their norms. With Parkinson out and Adams gone, Higbee (0.181 EPA per target) is the natural middle-of-the-field outlet beside Nacua.

nextGame.watch: His intended air yards: a return toward 7-plus means the arm is fine; another sub-5 day confirms a limited passer.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume should hold. The Rams pass more than situation predicts, he plays every snap when healthy, and the protection is excellent. The efficiency of the 2025 season is not coming back while the deep game is missing, and it can't fully return until Adams is back from IR (estimated late November) and the arm is right. Expect something like 225-265 passing yards and 1.4-1.9 touchdowns a game, with the interception rate easing slightly toward his career norm but staying above last year's.

The red-zone touchdown rate is the piece most likely to cool. The short-game accuracy and sack avoidance are the pieces most likely to last. If the soreness lingers or worsens, the floor drops quickly, because the recent three-game stretch, around 190 yards and negative EPA, is what the limited version looks like.
swingFactors: Right-arm soreness and whether his depth of target recovers
Davante Adams' return from hamstring surgery
Tight-end health with Parkinson out and Ferguson returning

confidence.note: Eight-game sample, with an arm injury and Adams' absence muddying the recent slide.
